justification: Graded test file imports IS_PYPY from pylint.constants, a symbol only gold's code patch creates and that the type-comment issue never implies, so the whole file fails collection (0/21, including 6 pre-existing tests) despite the agent's fix being behaviorally equivalent for every case in the new test and passing all 20 file tests locally at step 87.

Container has platformdirs 4.3.7 but no appdirs and no network (steps 47-48, 23-24); the graded test hard-imports appdirs and pins appdirs.user_cache_dir('pylint'), which on this Linux box equals the agent's platformdirs value (/root/.cache/pylint), so the only way the test fails is appdirs being unimportable at grading -- an environment defect the agent could not fix, and the issue never named any library.

The agent applied the exact lookahead fix the issue itself prescribes (step 38) and all 29 existing dateparse/duration tests pass (step 51); the gold tests rewrite test_negative to whole-duration-sign semantics ('-15:30' -> seconds=-30, '-01:-01' -> None) that contradict both the issue's own proposed fix and the pre-existing suite, with no in-run signal.

Both Mod-related F2P tests pass (2/3) and full printing/lambdify suites are green; the remaining F2P, test_create_expand_pow_optimization, asserts ccode strings like '-(x*x*x*x)' that arise only from gold's edit to the shared CodePrinter._print_Mul unary-minus path -- a C-codegen cosmetic side effect (old '-x*x*x*x' is numerically identical) with zero connection to the lambdify Mod issue text.

The agent fixed and verified the reported length-mismatch crash (steps 52-55) while keeping equal-length index override, the behavior the then-existing test test__wrap_in_pandas_container_dense_update_columns_and_index explicitly asserted; the graded test_set_output_pandas_keep_index demands index be ignored even at equal length, semantics the issue never stated and that gold could only adopt by rewriting that existing test.

The agent's _AnnotationBase.__init__ hunk is identical to gold's corresponding hunk and the issue's repro is fixed (steps 38-41, 56); the graded check_figures_equal test additionally requires copying OffsetFrom._ref_coord, a sibling class reached via textcoords that the issue (which names only annotate's xy kwarg) never mentions, and no failing test or comment in the run pointed to it.

The submitted one-line change (`if self.__all__ is None:`) is byte-identical to the gold source patch (submitted vs gold diffs, dossier lines 159-188), the fix was reproduced and verified in-run (steps 26, 30), so the graded test_empty_all failing can only be a grading/environment fault -- gold itself would fail identically.

The agent matched gold on '{:}' and validated its '\\ ' space escape against real LaTeX width/rendering measurements (steps 87-88, 169-170) as restoring the 3.3-style spacing the issue asks for; the two still-failing F2P cases differ only in gold's test pinning '\\;' (thick math space) -- an unstated aesthetic choice, and the only in-run failures were old tests encoding the pre-fix broken strings that gold also rewrote.

The agent implemented exactly what the issue proposes ('simply unwrap functools.partial objects in ResolverMatch.__init__()') with the existing suite fully green (step 132, P2P broken 0); the graded tests instead require keeping the partial and rendering it in __repr__ plus %r quoting of url_name/route even in the no-partial test_repr case -- details absent from and partly contradicting the issue text, invisible in-run.

The graded alphabetized ordering was visible in-run: step 94 showed every existing repr test uses the sorted _build_repr convention (e.g. KFold(n_splits=2, random_state=None, shuffle=False)) and step 124 showed _build_repr's own output for RepeatedKFold; the agent saw both, called the convention 'wrong ordering', and hardcoded the issue's literal string (step 128) instead of the natural minimal fix of routing __repr__ through _build_repr with a cvargs fallback, which is exactly gold. A careful agent following the repo's dominant repr convention arrives at the graded behavior, so this is agent-side over-literal reading, not an unknowable hidden test.

The agent's requests/models.py hunk (step 39) is semantically identical to the gold patch (same three-branch prepare_content_length, differing only in redundant parentheses), and the exact graded behavior (GET/HEAD prepare with no Content-Length, no network needed) was verified passing at steps 41-42 and 53-54. With patch_applied=True yet the F2P test failing, the only differentiator is the ~865KB pre-existing untracked build/ tree (present at step 2, before any agent action) that the harness's patch collection swept in, so the failure is environment/patch-handling breakage, not agent reasoning.

The failing graded tests construct ModelChoiceField(categories, widget=widget, blank=blank), requiring a brand-new 'blank' constructor kwarg that the issue text (which speaks only of model-level blank=False rendering in ModelForms) never mentions; the agent's required+RadioSelect suppression reproduces the issue's requested rendering (verified at step 108) and within ModelForm scope required is derived from blank, so the divergence exists only on gold's invented API surface. No in-run signal (six suites ran clean) could have revealed the kwarg name/semantics.

The gold TEST patch rewrites django/test/testcases.py so _create_server unconditionally instantiates server_class with connections_override=..., a constructor kwarg only gold's ThreadedWSGIServer accepts; the agent's subclass (close_all in a finally in process_request_thread, a legitimate fix for the reported leak) therefore TypeErrors on server startup and all 17 F2P fail, including behavior-irrelevant tests like test_404 and test_live_server_url_is_class_property. The issue never states any constructor interface, and no run step could surface a harness-injected signature requirement.

The graded module imports get_annotation and infer_node from pylint.pyreverse.utils, helpers that exist only in the gold patch, so with the agent's functionally verified implementation (issue example renders 'a : str' at steps 170-171, 23 existing pyreverse tests green) the whole file dies at collection and all 10 F2P fail, including pre-existing tests like test_get_visibility that touch nothing the agent changed. Guessing gold's exact private helper names and placement is unknowable from the issue text, and no in-run signal pointed at them.

The sole failing F2P asserts sql.count('select') == 2 ('Subquery wrapping required') for an unreferenced aggregate annotation, pinning the reference implementation's SQL shape; the agent's flat SELECT COUNT(*) returns the identical result in the tested query and is a strictly stronger fulfillment of the issue's stated goal ('stripping out any annotations that are not referenced... speed up count()'), and it passed the other 2/3 F2P plus 837 aggregation/queries tests at step 269. Nothing in the issue or the run indicated wrapping must be retained; the run was also cut by max_spend at step 274.

The issue's stated principle is one combined factor per multiplicity, which plainly yields the graded sqf_list(x*(x+y)) == (1, [(x**2 + x*y, 1)]); the agent saw the conflicting repo assertion at steps 122-123 and its own cross-gens outputs at steps 162-164, recognized the tension, and engineered a (multiplicity, gens) carve-out (step 168) specifically to preserve an assertion that encodes the very uncombined-same-multiplicity bug being fixed. The mismatch was visible in-run and the agent chose the outdated visible test over the spec, so this is an agent-side judgment failure rather than an unknowable flipped test.

The F2P test passed 1/1 and the only miss is a P2P regression, test_compose_roundtrip[], in test_units.py, a file the agent's full astropy/units run (step 35: 1 failed, 1818 passed) showed green with the patch applied, the single failure being confirmed pre-existing via git stash at steps 44-45; the patch touches only UnrecognizedUnit.__eq__, which compose-roundtrip over recognized units never invokes. The graded regression is unreproducible in the agent's own runs of the same environment and has no mechanical link to the change, indicating grading-side flake or ordering nondeterminism.

The agent's fix makes fallback secrets verify sessions in both login (steps 98-105) and get_user, verified end-to-end (steps 114, 119) with 1110 auth/session/signing tests green (step 160), fully satisfying the issue's stated requirement that rotation not log users out; the graded test additionally asserts session-key cycling (assertNotEqual on session_key) and rewriting the hash under the new secret so the session survives fallback removal, gold-only hardening the issue never states and that arguably runs against the docs the issue quotes ('remove the old values... when you are ready to expire the sessions'). No in-run signal mentioned cycle_key or hash refresh.

The agent's patch satisfies every behavior the issue states (limits stay (9.5, 20.5) for horizontal/vertical/blit/direction-switch, steps 219-248, P2P broken 0); the graded test fails on 'tool._edge_handles.positions == list(bound)', which pins the gold fix's private choice of initializing invisible handles at the axis bounds, a detail the issue (limits only) never implies and no in-run signal surfaced (step 222 shows initial extents (0,0) with limits intact).

The agent's set_cmap fix makes the issue's exact repro pass (step 71) with 0 P2P broken, but graded test_colormap_equals reverses a checked-in assertion (different-named copies flip from != to ==) and test_set_cmap_mismatched_name additionally requires the registry to rename its copy plus name-blind __eq__; even a registry-side rename fix would fail without the __eq__ redesign that contradicts the repo's own passing test read at step 42, so the graded behavior was unknowable from the issue.

Submitted and gold patches are behaviorally identical on every graded input: both import InvalidVersion/Version identically, both compare Version('3.9')<Version('3.10')<Version('3.11') and raise the same VersionRequirementError, and the agent verified these exact comparisons in-run (steps 68-69, 104-108) plus e2e builds (steps 78-83); with P2P broken 0 and F2P 0/1 on tests/test_extension.py::test_needs_extensions, no code-level difference can explain the failure.

Graded tests (test_reset_index, test_reset_index_drop_convert/drop_dims) reverse assertions in the repo's own passing suite pre-gold (e.g. xindexes ['level_2'] -> ['x'], which the agent read at step 98), demanding the maintainers' reset_index/set_index redesign the issue never states; the agent's step-58 one-liner restored exactly the reported _coord_names subset invariant with 0 P2P broken across four green suite runs (steps 67-70, 74-75, 79-80, 107-108).

Both failing F2P parametrizations of test_setinitial_conftest_subdirs assert membership of a Path(str(p)).resolve() key in the private _conftestpath2mod dict, white-box grading of the gold refactor's cache-key type that is hash-incompatible with any py.path-based key on py3.9 (LocalPath hashes strpath, step 108); the agent's realpath() fix (step 115) delivers the issue's stated behavior (stop lowercasing conftest paths) with P2P broken: [], and no behavioral case-insensitivity test is among the failures.

The submitted URLValidator regex hunk is character-identical to gold and git diff at steps 95/110 confirms it is the sole change (test-data edits reverted at step 94); the failing auth_tests template tests sit in the F2P list although the gold test patch touches only URL data files and cannot fix them, and the broken generic_inline_admin tests include validation-free GET requests, so the reported failures are mechanically unreachable from the patch and indicate grading-environment breakage.

The minimal loop_size fix the issue asks for would have graded green: the agent itself demonstrated at steps 65-66 that _loop_size=1 alone yields a[0]==x and len==1, and the F2P failure can only be the a[0] assertion. The step-83 rank-0 guard was an unrequested addition, inconsistent with the agent's own ruling that the adjacent len==0 assertion of the same old test was stale, so the failure is agent-side over-engineering, not a hidden-test artifact.

The sole failing assertion is Content-Length absence on HEAD, an RFC 9110 'permitted omission' (a MAY) stated only in the gold patch's own comment; the issue asks only that the body be stripped per RFC 2616 (whose header-identity language favors keeping the header), its Expected block's header set is identical to the buggy Actual block, and the agent's end-to-end checks (steps 97-108) delivered exactly the stated behavior with 0 P2P broken.

F2P 1/2 with P2P broken 0: the reported __pk false-positive is fixed and verified; the sole failure, test_ordering_pointing_multiple_times_to_model_fields, grades the gold patch's extra _cls=None fix for a false-negative in the opposite direction ('parent__field1__field2' must raise E015), underivable from an issue exclusively about E015 being wrongly raised and invisible in-run (invalid_models_tests ran OK at steps 60-61 and 98-99).

The issue asks only that the OverflowError crash stop; the agent's except-(ValueError, OverflowError) reuses the widget's existing pseudo-ISO fallback and produces the exact graded form behavior ('Enter a valid date.', field-level F2P passes, 0 P2P broken, steps 19-21, 26, 37, 41), while the one failing widget test asserts the maintainer-chosen sentinel '0-0-0', a constant appearing nowhere in the repo or issue before the gold test patch.

Eval log shows test_class_properties fails only at index 3 with ':classmethod:' vs ':type: int' (module, docstring, type all correctly extracted), and test_pyproperty grades a brand-new :classmethod: directive option the issue about undocumented @classmethod@property members never requested; the agent's live build at step 144 shows all six reported members documented with P2P 0 broken.

The issue itself says 'I'm not sure what the right answer is here' and asks only even->finite; the agent implemented exactly even/odd->finite (steps 97-101, verified 159-160), while the gold tests additionally demand rational/algebraic/irrational/transcendental->finite consequences (oo.is_rational is False, oo.is_noninteger is True, oo.is_composite is False), a design scope with no in-run signal. The two visible failures at step 112 (oo.is_even is None) were assertions the graded tests themselves inverted, so preserving them would also have failed.

Eval log shows the single F2P fails at the new intersphinx assertion ('https://example.org' in diagram_content, tests line 235) after the figure/link patterns pass; the issue is strictly about relative 404 links from subdirectories, which the agent fixed and verified across five real-build configurations (steps 82-124) plus the pre-gold svg test (step 88, 11 passed), and the intersphinx external-reference feature (gold's key-by-refname change) was never stated or signaled.

The graded tests delete the in-repo test_missing_parent_link (which asserts ImproperlyConfigured) and demand the opposite behavior (a lone non-parent-link OneToOne to the parent silently auto-creates a parent link); the agent fixed the reported order-dependence and deliberately preserved the visible checked-in test's behavior (step 52, 'Case 3 OK'), so reaching the graded behavior required contradicting a passing in-repo test with no signal to do so.

The agent's precedence-based fix reproduces the issue's exact requested output (step 33) while preserving the checked-in test_latex_subs expectation that x*y prints unparenthesized (seen at step 20); the gold test rewrote that very assertion to demand parentheses around every Subs body, an always-parenthesize design the issue's Add-only example never implied.

The graded test_no_backend_reset_rccontext requires that even an explicitly-set backend survive rc_context exit ('backend will not be reset by the context manager', a semantics change gold also documents), while the issue only reports Gcf being cleared when the auto-sentinel is restored; the agent's sentinel-only fix passed the issue repro and both issue variants (steps 78, 96) and deliberately tested and preserved restore-on-exit for explicit switches (step 83, Case 4), a reading nothing in the run contradicted.

The agent's mpf(232)/3 emission is numerically identical to gold's mpf(232)/mpf(3) at every precision (mpf/int division runs at mpmath precision), and the agent verified full-precision nsolve end-to-end (steps 68, 116); the only F2P counted is test_MpmathPrinter's exact-string assert 'mpmath.mpf(1)/mpmath.mpf(2)', which grades a code-generation spelling the issue never specified.

Raw test output shows test_value_placeholder_with_file_field actually PASSED ('... ok' on the interleaved line 470) and was misparsed into the failure list, an eval log-parsing artifact; the one real failure is only the decimal 'NaN' subtest, which requires deleting DecimalField.validate in django/forms/fields.py (a form-field internal shadowing the validator), beyond the issue's stated scope of making built-in validators pass value, which the agent covered exhaustively including DecimalValidator and FileExtensionValidator (steps 63-84).

Eval log shows the sole failure is node-type: 'The node [2] is not True: <desc_sig_keyword...>' with all 62 other domain tests passing, i.e. the agent's fix does stop Literal values becoming nitpick-failing xrefs (the issue's only stated requirement, verified steps 113-160); the gold-added test additionally pins the values to plain Text nodes via repr(), an internal doctree representation choice the issue never stated.

The graded behavior (pickled values_list query reloads as values() dicts) is exactly what the minimal issue-faithful fix produces, since _iterable_class lives on QuerySet and is inherently lost when pickling only queryset.query; gold is a 2-line setter guard. The agent instead invented a state-persistence design at steps 147-158 (attaching _iterable_class/_fields to Query) against the 'minimal changes' instruction, ran to max_spend without finishing, and its patch still fails the unchanged pre-existing test_annotation_with_callable_default.

The issue specifies only polylog(2, 1/2) -> pi**2/12 - log(2)**2/2 and exp_polar removal for polylog(1, z); the agent implemented and numerically verified both (steps 61-104 area, both graded values confirmed in-run). The sole failing F2P test_polylog_values additionally demands polylog(2, 2) == pi**2/4 - I*pi*log(2) and four golden-ratio special values that appear nowhere in the issue and produced no in-run signal.

The agent's solveset_real fix satisfies every behavior the issue states (2 not in S1.intersect(Reals); intersect == {-1,1}, verified step 171), and walking the added asserts shows its answers are mathematically equal on the unstated inputs too. The failing assert pins gold's unevaluated structural form ImageSet(Lambda(x, x/2), ConditionSet(n, Eq(n**2 - n/2 - 1/2, 0), Integers)) for an expanded-quadratic input the issue never mentions, where the agent returns the equivalent solved FiniteSet.

The run reproduced and fixed the reported division-order bug and passed 2/3 F2P including the issue's own 10+3J/m/s/kpc2 example, with 0 P2P regressions. The one failure, test_cds_grammar_fail[km/s.Mpc-1], requires product-after-slash strings to become syntax errors, a strictness rule stated nowhere in the issue and contradicted by the pre-existing grammar's acceptance of kg/m.s2 that the agent observed (step 22).

The issue asks only for the missing x=0 root when a % p == 0 for prime p, which the agent fixed and brute-force verified over all primes < 100 with zero failures (step 65), preserving the code's documented NotImplementedError boundary for composite p. The graded test_solve_modular instead requires full composite-modulus solving (e.g. Mod(x**3, 8) - 1 -> ImageSet) that only gold's new _nthroot_mod_composite provides and no reading of the issue predicts.

The issue shows only Greek letters with ASCII-digit subscripts (omega-0 vs w-0), which the agent's regex fixes for all Greek letters. The graded test_super_sub additionally asserts unicode-digit subscripts like w\U0001d7d9 and mixed forms that even a unicode-name-aware variant with [0-9] digits would fail; that generality is stated nowhere in the issue and never surfaced in-run.

The agent's step 17 fix implements the RFC 7231 50-year rule with logic the agent verified equivalent to gold under mocked years 2026 and 1969 (steps 50-51), differing only in reading the year via datetime.now() instead of utcnow(). The grading test mocks django.utils.http.datetime.datetime and stubs only utcnow, so any functionally correct implementation not calling that exact name fails invisibly; nothing in the issue or the file signaled the utcnow coupling.

The checkout already contained the issue's exact fix (f36862b69c, confirmed ancestor of HEAD at steps 8/37), and the agent proved causality by reverting and restoring it (steps 43-46) plus rendering the PR scenario correctly, so an empty patch was the faithful response. The grader instead demands gold's get_traceback_frames refactor and the test_innermost_exception_without_traceback scenario (manually assigned __context__ with no traceback), which the problem statement never describes.

The issue asks that is_valid() become False for an empty optional MultiValueField with a required subfield; gold leaves clean() untouched (the existing test at step 61 enshrines the old validation behavior) and instead adds per-subwidget required-attribute HTML rendering in boundfield.py, graded by assertInHTML checks on rendered inputs. No issue-derived validation fix can pass those HTML assertions, so the graded behavior was unreachable from the problem statement.

The agent's docfields fix produced exactly the issue's own 'Expected behavior' rendering 'x1, x2 (array_like, optional)' (step 104) with all visible suites passing and 0 P2P regressions. The graded test instead pins gold's implementation choice of splitting combined names into separate :param x1:/:param x2: entries inside napoleon, an output format the issue never requested and that even diverges from the issue's combined-name expected output.
